title: Optimal Collision-Variance Potentials, Minimal-Degree Newton-Binomial Filtering, and Exact Modular Coset-Halving Certificates for Deterministic Subexponential Discrete Logarithms
abstract: In a breakthrough of November 2026, Liu, Zhang, and Ren established the first deterministic subexponential-time algorithm for the discrete logarithm problem (DLP) in both prime-order elliptic curves E(F_p) and multiplicative prime fields F_p* (conditional on Cauchy-Hermite Boolean tensor contraction), combining Stage-I conditional-expectation derandomization of a collision-variance potential with fixed penalty lambda = 64 and thresholds B = 4096, A = 16, and Stage-II counterexample extraction via a degree-(4w + 2) nonnegative Newton-Binomial filter Q(X) coupled with Hermite normal form (HNF) modular coset halving. We establish three sharp theorems backed by 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems and 16 zero-float certificates. First, via two one-line perfect-square identities requiring zero calculus, we derive the exact global optimizer lambda* = c_0 / (sqrt(c_1)(1 - sqrt(c_1))) achieving maximum certified sumset density delta_max = (1 - sqrt(c_1))^2 / c_0, compressing the Stage-I threshold 64x (to A = 4, B = 64, lambda = 9, delta = 4987/9549 > 1/2, where LZR's fixed lambda = 64 collapses to 0.2876 < 1/2) and up to 146x-227x under the sharp binomial bound (1 + 1/(Bm))^m <= B/(B - 1). Second, we prove that LZR's extreme roots j = +/- w are strictly unreachable on [-w(M_lab - 1), w(M_lab - 1)] for all w >= 2, reducing the filter degree by 4 to 4w - 2 = 8m - 2 (saving 4 series terms and 4*ceil(log2(2w M_lab + 2)) bits in P_0), and prove unconditionally that 4w - 2 is the exact minimal degree among all real polynomials separating congruent from non-congruent integers. Third, we certify composite-modulus HNF coset halving, tighten LZR's Neumann M-matrix determinant bound via Fischer-Hadamard 0 < det(H_N) <= prod(w + 1 - D_ii) <= (w + 1)^N, and verify end-to-end deterministic zero-float DLP/ECDLP recovery on F_23*, F_47*, E(F_17), and E(F_23).
